correctness.rationale: An independent exact integer enumeration on all 22 listed 4D lattice vertices restricts a GL(4,Z) stabilizer by known vertex differences to 52 candidate (Ae1,Ae2) pairs and 12 (Ae3,Ae4) pairs, 624 cases total; determinant and complete vertex-set checks yield only I and displayed involution T. Independently enumerating primitive supporting hyperplanes from 4-vertex combinations yields 26 primal and 22 polar facets, with 72/68 distinct two-faces, size histograms (50 triangles,21 quadrilaterals,1 hexagon)/(38 triangles,26 quadrilaterals,2 pentagons,2 hexagons), and 20/26 parallelogram unit-square faces. For the 26 polar square-diagonal columns, exact rational elimination gives rank 18 and exactly two coloops, exchanged under T transpose. The signed action has domain ± eigendimensions 14 and 12, image ± ranks 9 and 9, and therefore kernel ± dimensions 5 and 3. All exhaustive calculations were run as a separate independent implementation; symmetry is of lattice polytope/fan, not a generic anticanonical hypersurface.

value.rationale: The exceptional mirror pair is singled out by a singularity/smoothability dichotomy, making its exact lattice symmetry and action on node relations natural finite invariants. The 5+3 kernel character and exchanged coloops refine known eight-dimensional dependency data and can constrain equivariant deformation questions, even though they do not themselves prove a smoothing theorem. Exhaustive computation of a motivated fixed finite object can be scientifically meaningful.
